item.title: Implement ledger.py per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief:
Operator's words (authenticated local operator): "Implement `ledger.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Goal: make ledger.py implement SPEC.md exactly. Read SPEC.md in the repository first; it is the source of truth for the API, the error cases and the boundary cases.

Constraints:
- Preserve the documented API (names, signatures, return values) exactly as SPEC.md states.
- Handle every error and boundary case SPEC.md specifies; raise the specified errors, not generic ones.
- Use only the Python standard library.
- Keep existing tests passing; extend test_ledger.py (or add focused test cases) covering each specified error and boundary case, not only the basics.
- Follow the repository's style. Keep functions small and explicit; validate inputs at the API boundary.
- Commit the work on the item's branch with a clear message. Do not add attribution lines.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every requirement in SPEC.md is implemented, and a test exercises each specified error and boundary case.
- The full test suite passes (run it with the standard library test runner that the repository uses).
- No behaviour outside SPEC.md is changed.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier; unchanged

pr.body: Approach: ledger.py holds a private dict copied from the input, guarded by one threading.Lock; transfer validates the amount, then both accounts (KeyError), then applies the same-account / insufficient-funds / overflow rules under the lock. Snapshot copies under the lock. Single lock means opposite transfers cannot deadlock. Tests: test_ledger.py extended (37 total) covering every SPEC error and boundary case, plus two thread tests with bounded joins that re-raise worker exceptions. Check: python3 -B -m unittest -> 37 tests OK at head 5d4a051. Assumptions: non-string account names passed to transfer raise KeyError (treated as unknown accounts); built-in int checks use type(x) is int so bool and int subclasses are rejected. Standard library only.
pr.summary: made Ledger implement SPEC.md. now validates balances and amounts at the boundary, raises ValueError or KeyError as specified, and serialises transfers and snapshots with one lock. before: stub raising NotImplementedError; now: 37 tests pass

agt_01M8GP47HJP98043TGXM8N1NB4:2.description: Only a non-string source is tested for KeyError; a non-string destination has no test. at test_ledger.py:124
